category: アクセス制御、データ保護、インシデント対応
title: External Accounts and Encryption
prompt: An object in an account A S3 bucket is encrypted with an account A customer managed KMS key. Both the bucket and a role in account B allow GetObject, but the role receives a KMS access denied error. You want to preserve the S3 permission.

choices.text: Add only kms:Decrypt to the IAM policy in account B
choices.explanation: This does not work unless the key-owning account also permits external use.

choices.text: Check only GetObject for the external role
choices.explanation: Permission to read the object does not grant permission to decrypt it with KMS.

choices.text: The key owner's permission and the reader role's kms:Decrypt permission
choices.explanation: For cross-account access, check both the key policy and the IAM permissions of the consuming role.

choices.text: Register the external account ID in CORS
choices.explanation: CORS concerns browser origins and does not control KMS access.

learning.reason: For cross-account access, check both the key policy and the IAM permissions of the consuming role.
learning.concept: During remediation, first identify which key encrypted the object.

title: Bucket Access from the Organization
prompt: You want to automatically identify, in a bucket policy condition, an IAM role from an account that has newly joined as a member of AWS Organizations. Avoid listing individual accounts or describing OUs, and verify that the IAM principal belongs to the organization.

choices.text: aws:PrincipalOrgID
choices.explanation: It determines the organization to which the calling principal's account belongs.

choices.text: aws:PrincipalType
choices.explanation: It determines the principal type, but cannot exclude a principal of the same type from another organization.

choices.text: aws:ResourceOrgID
choices.explanation: It determines the organization associated with the resource, not the organization of the caller.

choices.text: aws:RequestedRegion
choices.explanation: It conditions the API request's Region and does not identify the principal's organization.

learning.reason: It determines the organization to which the calling principal's account belongs.
learning.concept: An organization condition is one boundary. Also restrict the required actions, target prefix, and principal role as needed.

title: Centralized Auditing of Operations
prompt: An audit team wants to retain management events from all members in a central logging account for the long term and automatically include new accounts. What should it use to prevent member administrators from stopping the audit configuration?

choices.text: Configure a CloudTrail organization trail
choices.explanation: It applies the trail across the member accounts and can be managed from the organization.

choices.text: Send only VPC Flow Logs from each subnet
choices.explanation: These are network logs and do not record management API calls such as IAM operations.

choices.text: Create a regular trail with the same name in each account
choices.explanation: Aggregation can be designed, but local management and onboarding new accounts remain issues.

choices.text: View each member's event history separately
choices.explanation: This requires checking each environment individually and does not configure delivery to a shared organizational log destination.

learning.reason: It applies the trail across the member accounts and can be managed from the organization.
learning.concept: In addition to the organization trail, design the destination bucket policy and log retention method.

title: Detecting External Sharing
prompt: During an audit of the organization, you need to determine whether S3 buckets can be shared with external principals. You want to detect potential access across the entire organization as the zone of trust, even when the access has never been used.

choices.text: Analyze S3 data events with CloudTrail
choices.explanation: This approach examines actual operations and does not identify unused permissions.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning
choices.explanation: This provides version management for data; it does not compare resource policies for external sharing.

choices.text: Use AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: This service does not evaluate external sharing.

choices.text: Use the external access analyzer in IAM Access Analyzer
choices.explanation: It can analyze external access allowed by resource policies based on their configuration.

learning.reason: It can analyze external access allowed by resource policies based on their configuration.
learning.concept: Distinguish the possibility of external access from evidence that access actually occurred.

title: S3 Retention
prompt: The retention requirement for audit logs is to retain a specific version of each target S3 object for seven years. You must prevent deletion of the version and shortening of the retention period even by a principal with significant administrative permissions in the AWS account that owns the objects.

choices.text: Use Object Lock in compliance mode
choices.explanation: Protected versions cannot be deleted or have their retention period shortened during the retention period.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail data events to monitor deletions
choices.explanation: Although this leaves an audit trail, it does not prevent operations during the retention period.

choices.text: Enable Versioning only
choices.explanation: This does not prohibit deletion by directly specifying a version.

choices.text: Use only Object Lock in governance mode
choices.explanation: A principal with appropriate permissions can bypass governance retention.

learning.reason: Protected versions cannot be deleted or have their retention period shortened during the retention period.
learning.concept: The protected resource is an individual version. Distinguish the currently displayed object name from the protected object version.

title: Detecting Malicious Activity
prompt: Across multiple accounts, you need to continuously detect unusual credential use and suspicious network connections, and responders must investigate the findings. Use AWS-managed threat detection instead of relying only on custom rules.

choices.text: Use Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: It detects threats from relevant data sources and generates Findings.

choices.text: Enable only Security Hub configuration checks
choices.explanation: Configuration compliance assessments do not replace an API or network threat detection engine.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to check only required tags
choices.explanation: This verifies static configuration compliance, not suspicious API behavior.

choices.text: Move the accounts into an OU in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: Hierarchical management alone does not enable threat detection.

learning.reason: It detects threats from relevant data sources and generates Findings.
learning.concept: Define separate investigation and isolation procedures for responding to GuardDuty findings.

title: Separating Third Parties for Delegated Roles
prompt: Multiple customers delegate audit roles to the AWS account of the same SaaS provider. You want to ensure that the provider does not accidentally assume one customer's role when another customer gives the provider its own role ARN.

choices.text: Use a role ARN with a difficult-to-guess name
choices.explanation: This does not prevent confusion if a customer knows the ARN.

choices.text: Require a unique sts:ExternalId for each customer together with the provider principal in the trust policy
choices.explanation: The provider prevents confusion by sending the ID corresponding to the customer that initiated the call.

choices.text: Use the same ExternalId for all customers
choices.explanation: This does not provide a condition that distinguishes customers on the provider's side.

choices.text: Reduce the session duration to 15 minutes
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the incorrect role assumption itself.

learning.reason: The provider prevents confusion by sending the ID corresponding to the customer that initiated the call.
learning.concept: ExternalId identifies customers in third-party delegation and does not rely on concealing the role ARN.

title: Restricting the Encryption Key Usage Path
prompt: A role can read SSE-KMS data in S3. You are reviewing the key permissions and want to prevent the same role from calling the KMS Decrypt API directly. Decryption through S3 must remain permitted.

choices.text: Limit the permission to cases where kms:ViaService is the S3 service in the target Region
choices.explanation: This condition allows only requests made through the corresponding integrated service.

choices.text: Allow the target role unconditionally in the key policy
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish requests made through S3 from direct access.

choices.text: Change only the TLS condition on the S3 bucket
choices.explanation: This does not affect authorization for the KMS API.

choices.text: Enable automatic rotation for the KMS key
choices.explanation: Updating key material and authorizing the request path are independent concerns.

learning.reason: This condition allows only requests made through the corresponding integrated service.
learning.concept: Also verify that no other unconditional permission remains in the key policy or IAM policies.

title: Restricting Key Use to a Specified Path
prompt: A role reads SSE-KMS logs in S3. You do not want the role to have permission to call KMS Decrypt directly. Allow decryption only through S3 in the target Region.

choices.text: Use kms:ViaService as a condition and allow Decrypt only through S3 in the target Region
choices.explanation: The condition can identify requests made through the service.

choices.text: Require TLS on the bucket
choices.explanation: This does not remove permission to call KMS directly.

choices.text: Grant the role unconditional Decrypt permission
choices.explanation: This would also allow direct calls.

choices.text: Enable key rotation
choices.explanation: This does not constrain the access path.

learning.reason: The condition can identify requests made through the service.
learning.concept: Check both the key policy and IAM policies for any other unconditional Allow statement.

title: Containing Already-Issued Role Sessions
prompt: Temporary credentials for an operational role have been compromised. Before investigating, stop the use of sessions that have already been issued while allowing legitimate new sessions after the cutover to be used.

choices.text: Revoke the role’s active sessions and apply an explicit Deny to requests that use tokens issued before the cutover time.
choices.explanation: The token-issue-time condition can reject older sessions.

choices.text: Disable one access key.
choices.explanation: Requests from already-issued sessions for an assumed role must be controlled separately.

choices.text: Shorten the role’s maximum session duration.
choices.explanation: This does not change the expiration of tokens that have already been issued.

choices.text: Modify only the role’s trust policy.
choices.explanation: This affects new role assumptions but does not directly revoke already-issued sessions.

learning.reason: The token-issue-time condition can reject older sessions.
learning.concept: Stopping new issuance and stopping the use of already-issued sessions must be considered separately.
